root_cause: Starlette 0.48 renamed HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY to HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT (RFC 9110) and made the old name emit a DeprecationWarning via module __getattr__. FastAPI imported the old constant at module import time in fastapi/exception_handlers.py and fastapi/openapi/utils.py, so under Starlette>=0.48 with pytest filterwarnings=error the import/usage fails, and the new name does not exist on Starlette<0.48.
best_solution: Stop depending on either Starlette constant name: replace every use with the literal value. In fastapi/exception_handlers.py drop HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY from the starlette.status import (keep WS_1008_POLICY_VIOLATION) and use status_code=422 in request_validation_exception_handler. In fastapi/openapi/utils.py remove the import line and change `http422 = str(HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)` to `http422 = "422"` in get_openapi_path. Same change in docs_src/handling_errors/tutorial005.py (drop `status` import, status_code=422). Upstream also bumped pyproject starlette range to <0.49.0 (stripped from the gold patch). Works on both old and new Starlette with no warnings; `grep -rn HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` must return only tests after the change.
acceptable_alternatives: Using try/except import of HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT with fallback would also work, but the statement explicitly says literal 422/"422". Editing docs_src and pyproject is optional for the hidden test; v4 passed without either.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_enforce_once_required_parameter.py: test_get_invalid asserts response.status_code == 422 (literal); test_schema fetches /openapi.json, which runs get_openapi_path and needs the 422 response key "422" with no NameError/DeprecationWarning; test_get_valid. No new API names or strings beyond the integer 422 / string "422".
locating_signals: Statement names both constants HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY / HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT and says 'updated all instances' to literal 422/"422"; a repo-wide grep for HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY finds exactly the gold sites (exception_handlers.py import+use, openapi/utils.py import+use, docs_src tutorial). Functions are not named but grep is decisive.
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6, v7 passed (identical core edits to gold in exception_handlers.py and openapi/utils.py; v6/v7 also bumped pyproject starlette to <0.49.0; none touched docs_src, which the test does not need). v8 FAILED: it removed the `from starlette.status import HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` import in openapi/utils.py but never changed the usage `http422 = str(HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)` at line 418, so test_schema hit NameError: name 'HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY' is not defined (1 failed, 2 passed). Trace shows the fixer emitted a malformed edit_file call (new_string='            http422 = "422"`,old_string:' with old_string swallowed into new_string) and repeated the identical malformed call ~180 times until the step budget ran out (221 steps, 3.2M prompt tokens, 271 s), never recovering and never running a post-edit import/compile check.
generalizable_lesson: For rename/replace-all tasks, grep the old identifier before and after editing and do not finish until the post-edit grep returns zero hits in source (tests excepted); removing an import while a use remains is a guaranteed NameError. After any edit batch, run `python -c 'import <pkg>.<module>'` or the relevant test to catch undefined names. In the harness: detect a tool call repeated with identical malformed arguments (missing required param) 2-3 times and force a strategy change (e.g., rewrite the line via a run_command sed/python one-liner or a whole-function replace) instead of looping to budget exhaustion.
